result:
I would make truth-seeking the default human instinct—stronger than tribal loyalty, status-seeking, or comfort.

Not “more education” in the institutional sense. Not mandatory philosophy classes. Just a deep, widespread rewiring of incentives and cognition so that people experience genuine satisfaction from updating their beliefs when evidence demands it, and genuine discomfort from clinging to flattering falsehoods. Conspiracy theories, demagoguery, and sacred lies would still exist, but they’d have far less purchase because the average mind would treat them the way a healthy immune system treats pathogens.

Everything else I’d want—better governance, faster scientific progress, less pointless suffering—flows more reliably from that single change than from any top-down redesign of systems. People who actually want to know what’s true tend to build better tools, better institutions, and better lives. The reverse is rarer.
